events.title: Columbus Sights Trinidad
events.description: On his third voyage to the Americas, Christopher Columbus sighted the island of Trinidad and named it after the Holy Trinity. He then explored the nearby Gulf of Paria and the coast of present-day Venezuela.
events.significance: Columbus's third voyage marked the first European encounter with the South American mainland, expanding Spanish knowledge of the New World and paving the way for further colonization.

events.title: Death of Ignatius of Loyola
events.description: Ignatius of Loyola, the Spanish priest and theologian who founded the Society of Jesus (the Jesuits), died in Rome. He was canonized as a saint in 1622.
events.significance: The Jesuit order he founded became a leading force in the Catholic Counter-Reformation and a major influence on education, missionary work, and science around the world.

events.title: Cornerstone of the First U.S. Mint Building Is Laid in Philadelphia (Approximate Period of Mint Construction)
events.description: Following the Coinage Act passed in April 1792, the U.S. government began establishing the first federal mint in Philadelphia, with construction of its first building beginning in July of that year.
events.significance: The Philadelphia Mint was the first federal building constructed under the U.S. Constitution and established a national currency system for the young republic.

events.title: Apollo 15 Astronauts Drive the First Lunar Rover
events.description: On July 31, 1971, Apollo 15 astronauts David Scott and James Irwin used the Lunar Roving Vehicle for the first time on the Moon, exploring the Hadley Rille and Apennine Mountains region.
events.significance: The rover greatly extended the range of lunar exploration, allowing astronauts to collect more diverse samples and conduct more extensive scientific investigations than on earlier missions.

events.title: Birth of J.K. Rowling
events.description: British author Joanne 'J.K.' Rowling, creator of the Harry Potter series, was born in Yate, Gloucestershire, England.
events.significance: The Harry Potter books became one of the best-selling book series in history, spawning a major film franchise and shaping a generation of readers worldwide.
